summary:
Public Law 118-66, the "Dr. Emmanuel Bilirakis and Honorable Jennifer Wexton National Plan to End Parkinson's Act" (H.R. 2365, enacted July 2, 2024), directs the Secretary of Health and Human Services to establish and carry out a National Parkinson's Project to prevent, diagnose, treat, and cure Parkinson's. Its operative mechanism is an amendment to Title III of the Public Health Service Act (42 U.S.C. 241 et seq.), adding a new Part W ("Parkinson's and Related Disorders") comprising a single new section 399OO, codified at 42 U.S.C. 280n.

Section 399OO(a) defines "Parkinson's" to encompass both Parkinson's disease and all other neurodegenerative Parkinsonisms (including multiple system atrophy, corticobasal degeneration, progressive supranuclear palsy, and Parkinson's-related dementia). Subsection (b) mandates the Project's establishment. Subsection (c) enumerates required activities: creation, maintenance, and periodic updating of an integrated national plan; the annual assessment under subsection (d); provision of estimates of current federal investment and needed investment; cross-agency coordination of research and services; encouragement of treatment development; improvement of early diagnosis and care coordination; review of Parkinson's impacts on patients, caregivers, and families; coordination with international bodies; and collaboration to avoid duplication of research.

Subsection (d) requires the Secretary, not later than 24 months after enactment and annually thereafter, to conduct an assessment of national progress, including priority-action recommendations and a description of implementation steps (including whether recommendations can be implemented under existing law).

Subsection (e) establishes and directs the Secretary to maintain an Advisory Council on Parkinson's Research, Care, and Services. Membership comprises Secretary-appointed federal experts from fourteen specified agencies/offices (CDC, ACL, CMS, NIH, AHRQ, VA, FDA, NSF, DoD, EPA, Office of Minority Health, IHS, Office of the Surgeon General, and other relevant agencies) plus 10 non-federal expert members with enumerated compositional requirements (patient advocates, caregiver, provider, researchers, specialists, nonprofit representatives). The Council must meet at least quarterly during its first two years and thereafter at the Secretary's discretion; convene an annual research meeting (first due within 24 months of enactment); hold open meetings; and, not later than 18 months after enactment and annually, report to the Secretary and Congress with specified content, including a catalog of federally funded efforts, priority-action recommendations, an evaluation of the national plan's implementation, and implementation steps.

Subsection (f) requires federal departments and agencies to share Parkinson's-related information with the Secretary, consistent with applicable disclosure obligations, to enable the subsection (e)(4) reports.

The bill contains no appropriation. Subsection (e)(5) terminates the Advisory Council at the end of calendar year 2035, and subsection (g) sunsets the entire section at the end of calendar year 2035.
